questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The city, the University and the culture of the people. In Italy I felt that all these aspects where fulfilled in regards to what I was looking for in my exchange.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I thought it was quite easy. University of Copenhagen and University of Milan was good at communicating and gave good response.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The administration at University of Milan was very helpful. They responded quickly and gave me the necessary information when needed.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I thought it was quite hard to find housing. I looked for a long time and it surprised me how expensive and difficult it was. My recommendation is therefore to start looking in good time and I can recommend the websites: Spot a home and Dovavivo. I lived myself at a dorm called Giovenale Aparto, which I would highly recommend even though it was a bit expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Start looking for apartments in good time! All the good ones goes quickly.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: At University of Milan you can change courses during the semester and actually up to two weeks before the exam. Because it is so different from University of Copenhagen I was very confused about it in the beginning, because I did not understand why the University did not inform anything about registration for courses until 1 week before semester start.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The Administration at the University was very helpful and responded quickly.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I changed many of my courses during the semester, so my first choices were actually not that successful. So in that aspect it was nice that you could change the courses during the semester if you e.g. was not happy about the course or the professor.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do not stress about before you are there! You will figure it out as soon as the semester begins.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses was very easy. There was no mandatory reading and they only demanded presence, but many of the professor's did not take attendance anyway. So I would not recommend that you go there for the academic experience, because it is quite different and easy compared to University of Copenhagen - both the level of the courses and the final exams.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very different. The professors chose themselves the material of the courses and how the exams should be.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: European Company Law, European Labour Law, Introduction to Italian Private Law in a comparative perspective, Constitutional Challenges in the EU, Comparative Contract Law, Fundamental Rights in the EU

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Comparative Contract Law, European Company Law and European Labour Law

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It was possible to go on a ski trip.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The ski trips!!!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: It is very easy to come around in the rest of Italy from Milan. I would especially recommend trips to Como Lake, Venice, Rome, Verona and Florence. The plain tickets from Milan to Sardinia and Sicily is also very cheap (500 DKK both ways)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I thought it was quite easy. The italian people are very open-minded and generous.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go out to local restaurants, bars etc. This is the perfect place to meet local italian people - because it is a central part of their culture.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find any.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The Italian people are very easy-going and relaxed and the eat and drink out a lot. There is just a really nice vibe every night in the city.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1) Look for a residence in good time, 2) Save up a lot of money to experience Milan and the rest of Italy, because there is so many options 3) Be patient with the information - it will come

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The University experience and all the nice people I meet from all around the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I did not have any bigger challenges during the stay, but of course it is always a big change to move to another country and find your everyday there, without your safe environment from home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
